target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (F : ArithmeticTheory) [F.RE] [𝗜𝚺₁ ⪯ F], Def3 F →
    ∃ _ : Theory.RE (F ∪ {Def7 F}),
      Def3 (F ∪ {Def7 F}).theory ∧ Def7 F ∈ (F ∪ {Def7 F}).theory ∧ Def7 F ∉ F.theory ∧
        Def7 (F ∪ {Def7 F}) ∉ (F ∪ {Def7 F}).theory

translation: Target is defined to be the following proposition. For every arithmetic axiom set F, assume that F is recursively enumerable and that every theorem of IΣ₁ is a theorem of F (literal inclusion of axiom sets is not required). If every sentence in F is true in the standard natural numbers, then the following holds. Let c be the arithmetic sentence saying that the Craig presentation of F does not prove a contradiction, and let G = F ∪ {c}. There exists a witness that G is recursively enumerable such that all four conditions hold: (1) every sentence provable from G is true in the standard natural numbers; (2) c is provable from G; (3) c is not provable from F; and (4) the arithmetic sentence saying that the Craig presentation of G, formed using that witness, does not prove a contradiction is not provable from G. The truth hypothesis concerns the axioms of F, whereas condition (1) concerns all theorems of G. Target defines this proposition; it does not prove it.

divergences.description: Lean models a machine by a recursively enumerable arithmetic axiom set, and production by derivability. It also fixes IΣ₁ as a sufficient lower bound on the first machine’s deductive strength. Lucas does not specify a machine representation or an exact arithmetic base.

Lean assumes every axiom of the first system is true in the standard natural numbers and asserts that every theorem of the enlarged system is true there. The passage speaks of producing a particular formula as true, without explicitly requiring or asserting global soundness. The target thus covers sound starting systems, not merely consistent ones.

Lucas leaves the enlargement open. Lean chooses a particular one: retain all the old axioms and add just the first consistency sentence as an axiom. Recursive enumerability of this extension stands for the existence of the second machine.

The consistency-sentence proxy is used twice, not just for the first machine. The second machine’s unprovable sentence says that its own Craig presentation is consistent. This is specific to the enlarged system, as required for the claimed role, but it is not literally the self-referential sentence constructed by applying Gödel’s diagonal procedure to that system.

judgement.summary: On the stated role-based reading, the target captures the passage: the extension is again effectively axiomatized, proves the designated sentence that the first system could not, and has a designated unprovable sentence of its own. It does so for sound arithmetic systems using consistency sentences rather than literal Gödel sentences.
